findings.description: The database password is rendered into EC2 user data and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data and the resulting file can be read by parties with instance, metadata-service, backup/image, or Terraform-state access, exposing reusable database credentials.

The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, assigning a public network endpoint. Although the shown security-group ingress is VPC-scoped, this unnecessarily exposes the database to internet-reachable network paths and expands the attack surface if security-group rules change or other paths are introduced.
The RDS instance explicitly sets storage_encrypted = false, leaving database storage, automated backups, snapshots, and replicas created from this instance unencrypted at rest.

This policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on every resource to the role attached to aws_instance.catalog_app_server. Compromise of that instance yields broad account-level control and data access, including likely privilege-escalation paths through EC2 and IAM-adjacent EC2 capabilities.
